text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The new board at the Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority has refused to implement a Z$6 billion accord signed by the government and Malaysia's YTL company for ownership of Hwange thermal power station unless the government renegotiates the deal to give it a majority shareholding, industry sources said this week.

- Zimbabwe's cabinet has directed information, posts and telecommunications minister Joyce Mujuru to respond through the government tender board to allegations of irregularities in awarding the country's second cellular phone tender.
- The chief executive of Zimbabwe's trade promotion body, Zimtrade, Morrison Sifelani, has resigned after accepting a severence package estimated at about Z$900,000.

- Uncertainty continues to hamper construction of Harare's new international airport, with contractors still awaiting the disbursement of Z$200 million in bridging finance while parliament is reluctant to approve Z$1.2 billion in loan funds.
- The government-owned Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe notched a 20 percent rise in net profit to Z$12.1 million in the year ended December 1996.
- Four managers at Leopard Rock Hotel in eastern Zimbabwe have resigned over the past two months, with the general manager also leaving under unclear circumstances.

- The expatriate general manager of Zimbabwe's national pension fund, the National Social Security Authority, Rory O'Shea, is leaving at the end of his contract in September after a turbulent two years with the organisation.

- Zimbabwean farmers are expected to harvest over two million tonnes of maize this year, enough to meet domestic consumption with some left over for export, but below the 2.6 million tonnes produced last year.
